en: Gallium is a solid metal at room temperature but melts into a liquid in your hand because its melting point is 29.76°C.
Rusting is a chemical change where iron reacts with oxygen and water to form iron oxide, actually increasing the total weight of the metal.
Oobleck, a mixture of cornstarch and water, acts like a liquid when poured but becomes a hard solid when you punch it.
Water is one of the only substances on Earth that expands when it freezes, making ice less dense than liquid water so it floats.
The glowing gas inside a fluorescent light bulb or a neon sign is actually plasma, the fourth state of matter.
Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide that skips the liquid phase entirely and sublimates directly into a thick, cold gas at room temperature.
Mayonnaise is an emulsion, a special mixture where oil and vinegar are forced to blend together permanently using egg yolk as an emulsifier.
Aerogel is a solid material made mostly of air, making it so light it can balance on a delicate flower without crushing it.
Heating sugar causes a chemical change called caramelization, breaking down the sweet crystals into new compounds that give caramel its brown color and nutty smell.
Graphite, the soft material inside your pencil, is a non-metal that conducts electricity surprisingly well because its carbon atoms share free-moving electrons.
The screens on calculators and digital watches use liquid crystals, a unique state of matter that flows like a liquid but has organized molecules like a solid.
Shining a flashlight through a glass of milk reveals the Tyndall effect, where suspended fat particles scatter the light beam so you can see its path.
